title: Perception gap correction with a mechanism manipulation and delayed follow-up
why: Fixes the power and design problems by concentrating on the only arm with signal and by isolating its mechanism, adding a delayed outcome to address the immediate-measurement limit.

power_target.basis: Observed Perception gap video effect of -2.3 points (SE 0.995 at n = 641); sizing to detect about -1.7 at 80% power allows for winner's-curse shrinkage.

rationale: In the source study the Perception gap video was the only arm with p<0.05 on the thermometer (-2.3 points, SE 0.995, n=641), while pooled undemocratic-practices support did not move (-0.015, CI [-0.044, 0.014]) and outcomes were measured immediately. This design tests whether the effect runs through corrected beliefs about the outparty, whether it replicates against a placebo video, and whether it persists and reaches democratic attitudes.
contribution: Separates perception-correction from generic video and attention effects, tests mediation via perceived outparty views, and measures persistence and downstream spillover.
hypothesis: The Perception gap video lowers outparty animosity (thermometer gap) more than placebo or control, mediated by reduced perceived outparty extremity; the effect partly persists at follow-up, with smaller or null effects on support for undemocratic practices.
primary_outcome: Affective polarization (in-party minus out-party feeling thermometer) immediately and at 2-4 weeks.
comparison: Perception gap video vs placebo video; Perception gap video vs statistics-only text; each vs control; mediation via change in perceived outparty views.
unresolved: The actual video files, wave 2 survey instrument and link, IRB approval number, and compensation must be supplied by the research team.

title: Perception gap video across partisanship and sample
why: Addresses the sample and framing limits: the original was one Lucid panel, only partisans, with heterogeneity tests too imprecise to interpret.

power_target.basis: Interaction contrasts need roughly 2x the SE of the main effect; observed SE 0.995 at n = 641 implies detecting about 2 points in subgroups at around 750 per cell.

rationale: The Perception gap video was the only arm with p<0.05 (-2.3 points, 95% CI [-4.3, -0.4], p=0.019, uncorrected) in a single Lucid panel with only partisans, and heterogeneity tests were too imprecise to interpret. This design replicates it in two sample sources across Democrats, Republicans and independent leaners with pre-measures.
contribution: Tests whether the Perception gap video effect on the feeling thermometer and undemocratic-practices support holds across party, partisan strength and sample source.
hypothesis: The Perception gap video lowers affective polarization relative to control, and the effect does not differ materially by party, partisan strength or sample source.
primary_outcome: Affective polarization: in-party minus out-party feeling thermometer after treatment; secondary: mean support for undemocratic practices.
comparison: Perception gap video vs control, with treatment x party and treatment x sample interactions, controlling for pre-treatment measures.
unresolved: Hosting of the Perception gap video file

title: Affect-to-democratic-attitude transfer test
why: Addresses the measurement failure: the original had a null on undemocratic-practices support with no way to tell whether affect failed to transfer or the intervention was too weak.

power_target.basis: Undemocratic-practices pooled CI [-0.044, 0.014] and arm SEs of 0.05-0.12; 900 per arm detects about 0.09 on that scale.

rationale: The source found a pooled thermometer drop of -0.8 (95% CI [-1.4,-0.2]) and a Perception gap video drop of -2.3, but no change in undemocratic-practices support (-0.015, CI [-0.044,0.014]). It cannot tell whether affect fails to transfer or the interventions were too weak. This design uses a strengthened intervention to produce a larger affect shift, then tests whether downstream outcomes move in proportion to it.
contribution: Separates failed transfer from weak dosage by testing whether randomized affect shifts predict undemocratic-practices support and a behavioural proxy.
hypothesis: Transfer: downstream change is proportional to the affect change induced by treatment. Independence: undemocratic-practices support and donation willingness do not change even when affect shifts substantially.
primary_outcome: Support for undemocratic practices (mean of four items), with the thermometer gap as the first stage.
comparison: Each treatment arm vs control on both outcomes; 2SLS with arm as instrument for post-treatment affective polarization; compare reduced-form effect with the effect predicted from the first stage.
unresolved: Hosting of the Perception gap video and the Patriotic article text.
